TIL If whole Milk was labeled like 2% Milk, it would be 3.5% Milk

These are the standards in the US for fat content in milk products:

80% Butter

45% Manufacturer's cream

36% Heavy whipping cream

30% Whipping cream or light whipping cream

25% Medium cream

18–30% Light cream, coffee cream, or table cream

10.5–18% Half and half

3.25% Whole milk or regular milk

about 2% 2% milk or reduced fat milk

about 1% 1% milk or low fat milk

0–0.5% Skim milk or nonfat milk
So if milk had the fat content of butter.... It would be butter?

Yes, pretty much different proportions of the same stuff. Butter is made by churning milk cream. Churning it separates butterfat (fats present in milk) and buttermilk (watery milk). Butter consist of fats, a little amount of milk protein and water.
